subject: Deal shaping: list price alignment and end-to-end credit routing
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@horizonsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal shaping: list price alignment and end-to-end credit routing

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. As we move toward a private offer, two items we need to lock down so procurement can finish the PO:

1) List-price vs PO discounting approach — Horizon asked whether the private offer will be anchored to a Redwood list price (and whether that list price is visible on the cloud marketplace). We typically publish a public list but provide private-offer savings that show as a committed discount.

2) Credit routing for channel/reseller uplift — your reseller (BluePeak) expects a pass-through credit on overages and usage true-ups. Procurement wants to confirm how credits are routed and whether a reseller netback shows on the invoice.

Attached a simple worksheet showing the proposed list-price reconciliation and two credit-routing options (one where credits flow through the marketplace invoice, and one where Redwood issues a separate reseller credit).

Can you confirm which option procurement prefers and whether BluePeak needs an invoice line-item for their margin? If procurement is ok with Option B (Redwood issues reseller credit), we can update the DocuSign and pricing sheet and push the PO to signature.

Thanks — copying Ben and Irene for channel and ops input.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0118

Attachments: horizon_mcap_pricing_sheet.xlsx, redwood_listprice_vs_po.pdf

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@horizonsys.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal shaping: list price alignment and end-to-end credit routing

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the note and the worksheet. A couple quick clarifying questions from procurement:

- Is Redwood's public list price required on the PO, or can we simply reference the private-offer unit rates? Our legal team prefers minimal public pricing references in the PO.
- For reseller credits (BluePeak), we need a defined cadence and evidence (invoice + audit stub) so their finance team can reconcile. A separate credit from Redwood to BluePeak is acceptable, as long as Horizon receives a single net cost on our side.

If you can sketch the operational flow for Option B (Redwood credit to BluePeak + Horizon receives net charge), that would help us finalize the internal approval. Also confirm whether the private-offer discounts are reversible if we hit overage thresholds.

Thanks — will loop procurement if we need formal language.

Tom
Sr. Procurement Manager
Horizon Systems
procurement@horizonsys.com

Subject: Re: Deal shaping: list price alignment and end-to-end credit routing

Tom —

Good questions. Short answers:

- The PO can reference the private-offer unit rates only; public list price does not need to be on the PO. We'll map the private-offer SKUs to the public catalog internally for billing, but Horizon doesn't need the public list on your PO.

- Option B operational flow (high level):
  1) Horizon is billed by the marketplace for the private-offer net amount (private unit rate * usage / committed seats).
  2) Redwood issues a separate credit to BluePeak (reseller) for the negotiated margin as a one-time reconciliation or quarterly true-up, depending on preference.
  3) Redwood provides a credit memo + audit stub to BluePeak and copies Horizon procurement for transparency.

We can include language in the DocuSign that the private-offer discounts are fixed for the initial 12-month term and that overage pricing will follow the agreed unit rates (no surprise step-downs). If Horizon prefers a quarterly true-up cadence for reseller credits, we can specify that too.

I've attached a revised pricing PDF that marks Option B as our recommended path and a short example showing how an overage event would be charged and credited.

Would appreciate confirmation from procurement on the true-up cadence (one-time, quarterly, or monthly).

Thanks — Naomi

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@horizonsys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal shaping: list price alignment and end-to-end credit routing

Tom / Naomi —

Looping in a short ops note from the channel/finance side: when we do Option B, we need to:

- Record a contra-revenue credit (reseller pass-through) on Redwood's books to ensure margin visibility.
- Establish an internal tag on the invoice that indicates which line items are private-offer and which are reseller credits (helps downstream reconciliation).
- Confirm BluePeak's invoicing entity and VAT handling if cross-border — that will affect whether credits are grossed up or netted.

From a commercial perspective, we recommend quarterly true-ups. Monthly creates too much noise for larger deals and one-time can be tricky if usage ramps unpredictably. Quarterly also aligns with our standard reseller payout cadence, so ops overhead is lower.

If Horizon confirms quarterly, we can draft the DocuSign clause and the credit memo template.

—Ben
Head of Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference
